newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end one percent higher on Novartis.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end one percent higher on Novartis.

text.p: Swiss shares closed near the day's highs on Wednesday, drawing strength from a three percent jump in index heavyweight Novartis, which climbed 76 Swiss francs at 2,428 francs.
Dealers said Novartis was in demand again after a recent fall. "The disappointment with sales figures is gone and people started buying the stock again," one dealer said.
The pharma company said last week that half year sales were up 19 percent, which was considered slightly below expectations.
One dealer added prospects were good. "The market just wants to go up," he said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) was up 87.4 points or 1.5 percent to 5,929.5. The day's SMI high was 5,930.2 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 50.18 points or 1.35 percent to 3,767.97 points.
Bourse volume stood at 2.43 billion Swiss francs. "6,000 SMI points are within reach, but we would nee bigger volumes to overcome that level," one dealer added.
Dealers said industrials were generally lifted by the firming dollar. Wall Street's rise also helped the market.
Roche certificates were up 115 francs to 14,750.
Among financials, UBS was actively traded, adding nine francs to 1,700.

One dealer said the market did not seem to reacting negatively to a U.S. court hearing set for Thursday, which could decide the future of lawsuits charging that Swiss banks hoarded billions of dollars of unclaimed assets from Holocaust victims.
